newsitem.title: VATICAN: Israel's Netanyahu to visit Pope next month.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu to visit Pope next month.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was quoted on Monday as saying he would meet Pope John Paul at the Vatican next month.

Netanyahu, who has not met the Pope since his election last May, said in an interview with Telepace, a Rome-based Catholic television station, that he had scheduled the meeting with the Pope two days ago.

"I will be in Rome at the end of January and on that occasion, naturally, I will visit the Pope and the Vatican," he said in the interview, an extract of which was released to the media ahead of broadcast.
The Vatican and Israel established full diplomatic ties two years ago, ending centuries of often hostile Catholic-Jewish relations. Both sides are still formally at odds over the status of Jerusalem.
Most states including the Vatican do not recognise Israel's claim to Jerusalem as its "united and eternal capital" following annexation of the Arab eastern sector in 1980.
Last Thursday, the Pope and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat discussed the Middle East peace process in a meeting at the Vatican.
